<thought>Based on the observed molecular ion at m/z 182.07, the molecular formula C₉H₁₀O₄ (exact mass 182.058 Da) fits the data. The 13C NMR shows an aldehyde carbon (~196 ppm) and several aromatic carbons, consistent with a benzaldehyde bearing an ethoxy substituent and two phenolic OH groups. The SMILES “CCOc1c(O)ccc(C=O)c1O” encodes this structure, is valid, and its formula matches the experimental mass. Therefore it is the most plausible structure for the sample.</thought>
<final_answer>CCOc1c(O)ccc(C=O)c1O</final_answer>
